import { Aside, CardGrid, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Your [`#[app::state]`](/build/sdk-macros/) is built from the collection types in
`calimero_storage::collections`. Each stores its entries as separate entities,
so a call writes only the entries it touches, and the access-controlled ones
check who may write when the run writes. An app's calls run one at a time on its
leader and the other replicas apply what each run wrote
([CRDT collections](/protocol/crdt-internals/)), so choosing a collection is
choosing a data structure, a cost and a write rule, not a merge.

<Aside type="note" title="Get returns an owned, read-only copy">
  Storage values are not resident in memory like a `HashMap`'s — every `get`
  deserializes a fresh copy, returned as a read-only `ValueRef<V>`. To mutate and
  persist, use `get_mut` or `entry().or_default()` (both write back on drop). To
  keep a copy, `.clone()` it. Mutating a plain `get` result does not compile —
  that closes the "edit a throwaway copy and lose the change" footgun.
</Aside>

## Type reference

| Type | What it is | When to use |
|------|-----------------|-------------|
| `UnorderedMap<K, V>` | Key→value map; each entry its own entity. No iteration order. | Default key→value store; O(1) point lookups. |
| `UnorderedSet<V>` | Membership set; each member its own entity. | Default set; O(1) membership tests. |
| `SortedMap<K, V>` | An `UnorderedMap` with reads in key order. | When you need range / prefix / pagination / sorted iteration. |
| `SortedSet<V>` | An `UnorderedSet` with reads in member order. | Ordered membership with range / prefix / pagination. |
| `IndexedMap<K, V>` | An `UnorderedMap`'s stored bytes, with queries on the fields the value type declares. | List views that filter, count or page by a field: "open issues, newest first", "notes of deal 7". |
| `Vector<V>` | Append-only sequence; `push` mints a stable element id. | Ordered lists where you append and index. |
| `FugueText` | Fugue text over run-length blocks; two runs typed at one spot never interleave. | Collaborative plain text. |
| `RichText<Sc>` | A `FugueText` plus write-once formatting marks. | One formatted body. |
| `RichDocument<Sc>` | Ordered blocks, each with kind, depth, attributes and a `RichText` body, written field by field. | Block documents: headings, paragraphs, lists. |
| `ReplicatedGrowableArray` | Text; characters ordered by neighbor + HLC. Two runs typed at one spot can interleave. | Apps that already store RGA text. |
| `LwwRegister<T>` | One value; a write replaces it. | A single scalar/field. |
| `Counter` / `GCounter` / `PNCounter` | Per-account slots summed at read. | Counts; `PNCounter` allows decrements. |
| `Authored<C>` | Any keyed collection `C` (`UnorderedMap`, `SortedMap`, `IndexedMap`) where each entry is owned by its inserter. | Shared data where users own what they wrote, read however `C` reads. |
| `AuthoredMap<K, V>` | `Authored<UnorderedMap<K, V>>`. | Shared map where users own their own entries. |
| `AuthoredSortedMap<K, V>` | `Authored<SortedMap<K, V>>`. | Shared map with hierarchical keys where reads are range / prefix slices. |
| `WriteOnce<C>` | `Authored<C>` whose entries can never be edited or deleted, even by their owner. | Signed messages, votes, an audit log. |
| `Moderated<C>` / `ModeratedOnce<C>` | `Authored<C>` / `WriteOnce<C>` whose entries a rotatable set of moderators may also delete. | Posts or messages where moderators remove spam. |
| `AuthoredVector<V>` | `Vector` where each slot is owned by its author. | Append-only log where authors control their entries. |
| `UserStorage<T>` | Per-user slots; each account writes only its own. | Per-user state; anyone reads, only the owner writes their slot. |
| `SharedStorage<T>` | Value guarded by a writer set, checked when the run writes. | Group-writable shared state with rotatable writers. |
| `Ownable<T>` | Single-owner cell (a `SharedStorage` with one writer). | Single-owner resource with transfer. |
| `PermissionedStorage<T, A>` | Writer-set cell with a custom authorization policy. | Fine-grained per-operation access (read/write/delete/admin). |
| `FrozenStorage<T>` | Content-addressed, immutable; key is `SHA256(value)`. | Immutable, de-duplicated blobs/documents. |
| `ContentAddressed<C>` | Any keyed collection `C` with `[u8; 32]` keys, content-addressed and immutable. | An immutable log you also filter or page, e.g. `ContentAddressed<IndexedMap<[u8; 32], Event>>`. |
| `Frozen<T>` | One value, written once by whoever created it; a change or a delete is refused. | A charter, a founding date, configuration fixed at `init`. |
| `AccessControl` | Role registry (admins + named roles) backed by `SharedStorage`. | Multi-tier authorization (admins, editors, ...). |
| `Registry<K, V, A>` | Claims owned by their claimants; verdicts written only by the authority `A`, each its own entry, the highest epoch then lowest order standing. | Usernames, seats, slugs: at most one owner per name. |

<Aside type="caution">
  These are the publicly re-exported types in `crates/storage/src/collections.rs`.
  `Counter` is an alias over a const-generic `Counter<ALLOW_DECREMENT>`:
  `GCounter` (increment-only, reads `u64`) and `PNCounter` (increment + decrement,
  reads `i64`). `WriterSetCell` and `FrozenValue` also exist but are the building
  blocks behind `SharedStorage` and `FrozenStorage` — reach for the higher-level
  types.
</Aside>

## The everyday types

- **`UnorderedMap` / `UnorderedSet`** — your defaults. Each entry is its own
  entity, so a call that sets one key writes only that entry; a
  `UnorderedMap<String, LwwRegister<String>>` is the pattern `apps/kv-store` uses.
- **`SortedMap` / `SortedSet`** — the unordered pair with reads in key order:
  `range(a..b)`, `prefix(p)`, `page(offset, limit)`, `first()`, and `last()`.
  A cluster node keeps no ordered index, so each of these reads loads and sorts
  every entry ([cost](/build/storage-complexity/#ordered-reads-and-indexes-on-a-cluster)).
  See `apps/sorted-kv-store`.
- **`IndexedMap`** — an `UnorderedMap` whose value type declares what it is
  looked up by, so a list view is a query by field. Derive the declaration and
  query by index name:

  ```rust
  #[derive(BorshSerialize, BorshDeserialize, AbiType, app::Mergeable, app::Indexed)]
  #[borsh(crate = "calimero_sdk::borsh")]
  #[index(status_created(status, created_at))]
  pub struct Issue {
      #[index] pub status: LwwRegister<String>,
      #[index] pub labels: LwwRegister<Vec<String>>,   // one row per label
      pub created_at: LwwRegister<u64>,
  }

  let newest_open = self.issues
      .query("status_created").eq("open").desc().limit(20).entries()?;
  let open = self.issues.query("status").eq("open").count()?;
  ```

  `eq` pins the index key's next component and `range` bounds the one after;
  on a compound index the free components order the result. A `Vec` field puts
  the entry in once per element and an `Option::None` leaves it out. Change an
  indexed field with `update(key, |v| ...)`, which keeps the indexes in step.
  The map reports itself as an `UnorderedMap` and stores exactly its bytes, so
  switching a field from `UnorderedMap` to `IndexedMap` needs no migration. A
  cluster node keeps no secondary index, so each query scans every entry,
  `O(n)` ([cost](/build/storage-complexity/#ordered-reads-and-indexes-on-a-cluster)).
  See `apps/indexed-issue-tracker`,
  and `apps/indexed-forum` for a compound index over a list and `IndexedMap`
  beside authored and set collections.
- **`Vector`** — append + index. `push` assigns each element a stable id, so
  iteration order is preserved across reloads.
- **`LwwRegister<T>`** — wrap any scalar. This is how you store a `String`,
  number, or enum inside app state (bare scalars are rejected by the state
  lint). `set` replaces the value; `get_mut` edits in place and writes on drop.
- **`Counter` family** — increments are tracked per account and summed on read.
  `GCounter` is increment-only; `PNCounter` also decrements.

<Aside type="tip" title="New collaborative text: use FugueText">
  `FugueText`, `RichText` and `RichDocument` keep two runs typed at the same spot whole instead of interleaving them, and cost less per keystroke.
  [Build a collaborative editor](/build/guides/collaborative-text/) shows how to wire an editor to them.
</Aside>

`ReplicatedGrowableArray` names each character by a `CharId` (HLC + sequence)
and orders the text by a deterministic walk over them. Two runs typed at the
same spot can interleave, which is why new text should use `FugueText`.

## Worked examples

A different real scenario for each everyday type — pick the one whose shape
matches what you are modeling.

**`SortedMap` — a live leaderboard.** Keys sort ascending by their *raw bytes*,
so to show highest scores first, store `u64::MAX - score` big-endian; the
top scores then come first:

```rust
// Leaderboard, highest score first. Big-endian is mandatory: otherwise 255
// sorts after 256, and `u64::MAX - score` inverts ascending order into a ranking.
let mut board: SortedMap<[u8; 8], LwwRegister<String>> = SortedMap::new();
board.insert((u64::MAX - score).to_be_bytes(), player.into())?;
let top_10 = board.page(0, 10)?;                       // sorts every entry, then takes 10
```

The same shape backs a time-ordered activity feed — key on a big-endian
timestamp and `range(since.to_be_bytes()..now.to_be_bytes())?` to read a window.

**`UnorderedMap` — an asset registry.** The default key→value store when every
access is a point lookup by id and iteration order never matters:

```rust
// id -> asset metadata; O(1) lookups, no ordering overhead.
let mut assets: UnorderedMap<String, LwwRegister<String>> = UnorderedMap::new();
assets.insert(asset_id.clone(), metadata_uri.into())?;
let uri = assets.get(&asset_id)?;                      // O(1), independent of size
```

**`UnorderedSet` — a moderation blocklist.** Membership is exactly what a
blocklist (or a tag set) wants: blocking an account twice leaves it blocked
once:

```rust
let mut blocked: UnorderedSet<String> = UnorderedSet::new();
let was_new = blocked.insert(account_id)?;             // false if already present
if blocked.contains(&caller)? { return; }              // reject the action
```

**`Vector` — an append-only audit log.** `push` mints a stable element id, so
insertion order survives reloads; read the whole log with a single `iter` pass:

```rust
let mut audit: Vector<LwwRegister<String>> = Vector::new();
audit.push(format!("{caller} granted role: admin").into())?;
for line in audit.iter()? { /* render oldest-first */ }  // one O(n) pass — never get(i) in a loop
```

**`Counter` — like / view counts.** Increments are tracked per account and
summed on read, so each like adds to its liker's own slot. Nest per id:

```rust
let mut likes: UnorderedMap<String, Counter> = UnorderedMap::new();
likes.entry(post_id)?.or_default().increment()?;       // one more in the caller's slot
```

**`ReplicatedGrowableArray` — a collaborative document.** A shared notepad
several people edit; build text with one bulk `insert_str`, never a
per-character loop (each call re-materializes the whole document):

```rust
let mut doc: ReplicatedGrowableArray = ReplicatedGrowableArray::new();
doc.insert_str(0, "Hello, world")?;                    // bulk — materializes order once
let text = doc.get_text()?;                            // deterministic walk over all chars
```

## Key types

Map and set entries are addressed by the **raw bytes of their key**, so a key type
must implement `AsRef<[u8]>` (the SDK's `StorageKey` requirement, alongside being
borsh-(de)serializable, `Eq`, and `'static`). A bare `u64` or an arbitrary struct has
no canonical byte form, so it is **rejected at compile time** — `insert` / `get` simply
won't accept it:

```rust
// Does not compile: `u64` is not a `StorageKey` — it has no `AsRef<[u8]>`.
let mut scores: UnorderedMap<u64, LwwRegister<String>> = UnorderedMap::new();
```

The fix is a thin **newtype** that wraps an already-byte-encodable representation and
forwards `AsRef<[u8]>` to it. This is the `apps/custom-key-store` pattern — and it is
also where you put key normalization or validation:

```rust
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, BorshSerialize, BorshDeserialize)]
#[borsh(crate = "calimero_sdk::borsh")]
pub struct Slug(String);

impl AsRef<[u8]> for Slug {        // the impl that makes it a valid key
    fn as_ref(&self) -> &[u8] {
        self.0.as_bytes()
    }
}

// Now compiles: `Slug: StorageKey`, so every key op is available.
let mut pages: UnorderedMap<Slug, LwwRegister<String>> = UnorderedMap::new();
```

In an owned collection (`Authored`, `WriteOnce`, `Moderated`, `ModeratedOnce`) a
key's `as_ref()` bytes must also be the **tail of its borsh encoding**, because
the storage layer recovers the key from the stored entry's bytes. `Slug(String)` is
(borsh writes a `String` as its length, then its bytes), and so are `Vec<u8>`,
`[u8; N]` and account ids; a key whose bytes are not is refused on insert.

The same shape works for an id newtype over `[u8; 32]`. For a numeric key, wrap the
**big-endian** bytes (`u64::to_be_bytes()`) so that — in a `SortedMap` — byte order
matches numeric order; see [Modeling your state](/build/state-modeling/) for why
little-endian keys sort incorrectly.

## Access-controlled collections

These add a write rule to a collection. The rule is checked when the run
writes, on the app's leader, against the caller's account; a write the caller
may not make is refused and nothing is appended, and the other replicas apply
the leader's diff without running it again
([Where the rule is checked](/build/permissioned-storage/#where-the-rule-is-checked)).
Because the rule lives in the type, it holds for every method that writes the
field, not only the ones that remember to check.

- **`Authored<C>`** — *per-entry ownership over any keyed collection*. The
  collection decides how entries are read, and `Authored` decides who may change
  them:

  ```rust
  posts:    Authored<IndexedMap<String, Post>>,   // filter, sort, count by fields
  comments: Authored<SortedMap<String, Comment>>, // threads as key ranges
  ```

  `insert` stamps the caller as owner, and `update` / `modify` / `remove` are
  refused for anyone else. Reads are the
  inner collection's own (`query`, `range`, `prefix`, `entries`), with `get`,
  `owner_of` and `owned_by_me` added. `Authored<C>` is `Guarded<C, Owner>`: one
  entry carries one stamp, so the write policy is a type parameter rather than
  wrappers that nest. `Authored<IndexedMap>` stores exactly an `AuthoredMap`'s
  bytes, so switching a field between them needs no migration. See
  `apps/indexed-forum`.

- **`AuthoredMap<K, V>` / `AuthoredVector<V>`** — *per-entry ownership*.
  `AuthoredMap` is `Authored<UnorderedMap<K, V>>` under its original name. Anyone
  can insert a new key (or push a new slot); the inserter is recorded as owner.
  Only the owner may `update` or `remove` (vector entries are tombstoned, not
  physically removed). Anyone can read. Use for
  shared maps/logs where users own what they contributed.

- **`AuthoredSortedMap<K, V>`** — the same ownership model with an ordered view,
  so a reader can `prefix` / `range` / `page` instead of walking everything.
  Identical in storage (it reports `CrdtType::UserStorage` like `AuthoredMap`),
  and it costs what `SortedMap` costs: on a cluster, each ordered read loads and
  sorts every entry.

  <Aside type="caution" title="An authored collection can be grown by anyone">
  On an authored collection the two halves of the ownership model compound:
  **anyone may insert under any key**, and **only an entry's own owner may ever
  remove it**. So a member acting in bad faith can grow the collection without
  bound and nobody else can shrink it, and every read that loads the whole
  collection pays for that. On a cluster that is every ordered read too, since
  the node keeps no index: a `prefix` slice of an `AuthoredSortedMap` loads and
  sorts every entry before it slices. Shard by the key readers ask for (one
  collection per topic, per channel) so a flood in one shard costs only its
  readers.

  Worked example in `apps/authored-sorted-kv-store`, with
  `workflows/authored-sorted-kv-store.yml` checking that authored state is read
  back by another account and that the owner gate refuses that account's edit.
  </Aside>

- **`UserStorage<T>`** — *per-user slots keyed by identity*. Each executor can
  only write its own slot (`insert` targets `env::account_id()`); reads are
  unrestricted (`get` for the current user, `get_for_user(key)` for any). Use for
  per-user preferences or state. See `apps/kv-store-with-user-and-frozen-storage`.

- **`SharedStorage<T>` / `Ownable<T>` / `PermissionedStorage<T, A>`** —
  *writer-set guarded*. The value lives behind a set of authorized writer
  identities. `SharedStorage` lets any current writer write; `Ownable` is the
  single-writer case with `owner` / `transfer_ownership`; `PermissionedStorage`
  takes a policy `A` (e.g. `OwnerAcl`, `WriterSetAcl`, `ProtocolAuthorizer`) for
  per-operation granularity (read / write / delete / admin). Writers are
  rotatable (`rotate_writers`), and the node checks each rotation after the run
  against the writer set it replaces. See
  `apps/kv-store-with-shared-storage`.

- **`AccessControl`** — a role registry built on `SharedStorage` whose writer set
  is the admin tier. Admins grant/revoke named roles (`grant(role, who)`,
  `has_role`, `grant_admin`, ...); a grant is checked against the admin writer
  set when the run writes. Use
  for multi-tier authorization.

- **`Registry<K, V, A>`** — *one owner per name*. Members `claim` a name into
  their own `Authored` entry; only the authority `A` writes verdicts: a TEE
  through a `TeeOnly` cell (`Tee`, the default), the admins through a
  `SharedStorage` cell (`Admin`), or nobody (`NoAuthority`, which reports
  contests). `status` is `Free`, `Pending`, `Owned`, `Lost` or `Contested`, and
  `owner_of` is `Some` only once a verdict names an owner. See
  [choosing a collection](/build/choosing-state/#unique-names-registry),
  `apps/name-registry` (`Tee`) and `apps/name-registry-admin` (`Admin`).

## Immutable / content-addressed

- **`FrozenStorage<T>`** — a map whose key is the `SHA256` of the value. Entries
  are immutable: no overwrite, no remove. `insert(value)` returns the hash;
  inserting identical content again stores nothing new. Use for
  archives, static assets, or any content-addressed immutable data. See
  `apps/kv-store-with-user-and-frozen-storage`.

- **`ContentAddressed<C>`** — the same rule over any keyed collection with
  `[u8; 32]` keys: `ContentAddressed<IndexedMap<[u8; 32], Event>>` is an
  immutable, de-duplicated log you can still filter and page. `insert(value)`
  returns the hash, an entry whose key is not its hash is refused, and
  nothing can update or remove one. `ContentAddressed<UnorderedMap<[u8; 32], T>>`
  stores exactly a `FrozenStorage<T>`'s bytes. A content-addressed value should
  be plain data, since its hash is taken over the bytes it is written with.

- **`WriteOnce<C>`** — owned *and* immutable: the inserter owns the entry, and
  nobody, the owner included, can change or delete it. A second, different
  value for one key seals the entry and `get` returns
  `StorageError::Conflicted`. Every listing
  of a `WriteOnce` or `ModeratedOnce` collection (`entries_with_owners`,
  `entries_by`, `my_entries`, `entries_at`, `entries`, and a sorted map's
  `keys`, `values`, `range`, `prefix`, `page`, `first`, `last`) returns a
  `Written<V>` per entry, `Written::Conflicted` for a sealed one, so a tally
  must count it. An `IndexedMap` query matches indexed values, and a sealed
  entry has none, so it never matches one. Use it when the key is the app's own
  (a message id) rather than a hash.

- **`Frozen<T>`** — one value rather than a collection: written in `init`, read
  with `get`, and there is no `set`. Its only writer holds a write-once
  capability, so a removal is refused, and a second value from its writer
  seals it (`get` returns `StorageError::Conflicted`).

See [Choosing state](/build/choosing-state/) for how these compare, and for
what protects the collections nested inside a guarded entry.

<Aside type="tip" title="Composing values">
  Collection values can be other collections. Nest them
  (`UnorderedMap<String, Counter>`) and each nested collection is written entry
  by entry. A map entry holding a plain struct is one entity, though: a write
  replaces the whole struct. See
  [Writing: the entry is the unit](/build/choosing-state/#writing-the-entry-is-the-unit).
</Aside>
